threads.body: [Style] This stream attribute is used only within the `server` package, so making both the class and constructor public exposes more API than necessary. Please use package-private visibility, consistent with the repository's least-access rule.

replies.body:
Addressed in 457c7b21a817fddeaf48049e62faf550c9a554af.

Analysis: Every reference to PekkoHttpServerRemoteAddress is in the server package. Package-private visibility keeps those callers working and follows the repository's minimal visibility rule.

Upsides: This keeps the stream attribute as a package implementation detail and avoids an accidental API.

Downsides: Code outside the server package can no longer reference or construct the class. No current caller does so.

threads.body: [Style] These comments say the helper is inlined into application packages, but both call sites use `@Advice.OnMethodExit(..., inline = false)`, so construction remains in the package-local advice class. Keeping this class and constructor public unnecessarily exposes an implementation detail; make both package-private.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: `TypeTransformerImpl` overrides the source annotation through `AdviceInliningPoolStrategy(poolStrategy, true)`. In classic advice mode, Byte Buddy therefore copies both advice bodies into Pekko classes. A package-private helper then causes `IllegalAccessError`, as the previous visibility change demonstrated in the `indy false` and latest-dependency CI jobs. The public class and constructor are required in that mode.

Upsides: This keeps socket remote-address attachment working in both advice modes and avoids suppressed advice failures.

Downsides: The helper is visible outside its package. It remains an internal javaagent class that is shaded into the agent artifact, so this does not expose an application API.

threads.body: [Testing] This new source-based server uses the default `h1c` protocol only, so it covers the `IncomingConnection.flow()` path for HTTP/1.1 but not the HTTP/2 source path claimed by the PR. The latter depends on `PekkoConnectionFlowAdvice` propagating the address into `Http2RequestParsingInstrumentation`, while the existing HTTP/2 test uses the higher-level `newServerAt(...).bind(...)` API and therefore cannot verify that interaction. Please add an HTTP/2-enabled `IncomingConnection` test using `h2c`.

replies.body: Pekko’s connection-source API does not support HTTP/2; enabling it explicitly falls back to HTTP/1.1. The existing `newServerAt(...).bind(...)` h2c test covers the supported HTTP/2 path through `prepareAttributes` and `Http2RequestParsingInstrumentation`. I corrected the PR description rather than adding an unsupported source-based HTTP/2 test.
